title: Wakapi
name: wakapi
description: Coding time tracker that works with the WakaTime editor plugins. Point them at your own server and get stats per project, language, editor and machine, plus badges you can put in a README. Source: https://github.com/muety/wakapi

env.name: WAKAPI_PASSWORD_SALT
env.label: Password salt (required)
env.description: Mixed into every password hash. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or nobody can log in.

env.name: WAKAPI_COOKIE_KEY
env.label: Cookie key
env.description: Keeps you logged in when it restarts. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32. Leave it blank and every restart logs everyone out.

env.name: WAKAPI_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the password salt before you deploy (openssl rand -hex 32 makes a good one), since the stack won't start without it, and keep it the same when you redeploy. Then open http://<your-host>:3100 (or whichever port you picked) and sign up. The first account is the admin. Sign-ups stay open, so once you've made yours add WAKAPI_ALLOW_SIGNUP = false to the stack's environment variables and update the stack. The setup page shows the ~/.wakatime.cfg lines for your editor's WakaTime plugin, with your API key. Invite links point at localhost until you add WAKAPI_PUBLIC_URL (like http://192.168.1.10:3100) there too. The logged-out front page loads one badge image from badges.fw-web.space. Everything lives in SQLite, in the wakapi-data volume. Docs: github.com/muety/wakapi
